claims.claim: review_transport provides the explicitly invoked read-only source-binding API and composes existing TASK-376/VP-02 validators without adding admission or scheduling authority.

The implementation checks configured canonical remote/main before and after observation, authenticates anchored commit/tree/path/blob identities and bytes, and derives TASK identity, revision and complete acceptance IDs from authenticated TASK content.

Explicit rejection paths cover ambiguous or wrong remotes, unanchored/stale sources, moved main, incorrect object/path/content identities, conflicting declarations and malformed, duplicate-key or oversized documents.

Authenticated documents pass through existing strict intake and complete mapping validators, preserving integration, fixture, worker, concurrency and ordering conditions; caller-supplied provenance labels cannot replace Git source bindings.

The frozen observation records exact source provenance while retaining UNESTABLISHED approval, semantic review, canonical verification, applicability and production authority, with KA-01 NOT_ACTIVATED.

Focused synthetic Git tests retain success, rejection, reordering, effect-trap and historical transport coverage. Collection-only diagnostics found 562 tests and 562 unique slash-normalized node IDs, including all nine negative path cases. The two colliding cases now have explicit disjoint IDs; their original values and assertions remain intact.
The source-binding document explains the authentication increment and remaining independent authority, full L1, VP-01, L2/L3 and KA-01 G3/G6 dependencies.

The permitted TASK surfaces are preserved. This repair changes only test parameter IDs, leaves the implementation, documentation and harness unchanged, and is committed as a clean descendant of the exact failed candidate. No push or canonical verification was performed.
